steps.title: Project Overview
steps.description: Start with the root README to understand the project's purpose: a complete three-body simulation and CTL-PINN training stack. This document outlines the four main components -- Brutus (high-precision N-body integrator), the Python simulation pipeline, the CTL-PINN (Curriculum-Trained Physics-Informed Neural Network), and reference code -- and their relationships. The dataset documentation provides the canonical specification for simulation data formats and known anomalies.

steps.title: Initial Condition Generation
steps.description: Every three-body simulation begins with initial conditions. The `generate_ics.py` script is the primary entry point for creating ICs using Sobol sequences for quasi-random sampling of the parameter space. It delegates to `ic_generation_utils.py` for core physics functions -- computing center-of-mass frames, scaling positions and velocities, and enforcing conservation constraints. These files define the vocabulary (masses, positions, velocities) that flows through the entire pipeline.
steps.languageLesson: Sobol sequences are low-discrepancy quasi-random sequences that fill a high-dimensional space more evenly than pure random sampling, reducing the number of simulations needed to cover the parameter space.

steps.title: Brutus Engine: High-Precision N-Body Integration
steps.description: The computational heart of the project. `main.cpp` is the C++ entry point that parses arguments, loads or generates initial conditions, and drives the simulation. `Brutus.cpp/h` implements the core integrator using the Bulirsch-Stoer algorithm with arbitrary-precision arithmetic -- essential for the chaotic three-body problem where numerical errors grow exponentially. This engine produces the high-fidelity trajectory data that the entire downstream pipeline depends on.
steps.languageLesson: The Bulirsch-Stoer algorithm is an adaptive extrapolation method for ODEs. It takes multiple steps at different resolutions and uses Richardson extrapolation to cancel lower-order error terms, achieving high accuracy in regimes where standard Runge-Kutta methods would require impractically small step sizes.

steps.title: Running Brutus at Scale
steps.description: Single simulations are not enough -- the dataset requires thousands of Brutus runs across different IC configurations. The runner scripts orchestrate batch execution: `run_brutus_both_type_simple.py` handles standard IC types, while `run_brutus_hierarchical_only_mac_gold_standard.py` runs the gold-standard hierarchical simulations that serve as ground truth for PINN training. These scripts manage the C++ binary invocation, output parsing, and error handling at scale.

steps.title: Metrics Extraction and Prescreening
steps.description: Once Brutus produces raw trajectories, the metrics layer extracts physically meaningful quantities: energy conservation, angular momentum, Lyapunov exponents, and close-encounter statistics. `calculate_metrics.py` (fan-out 26, one of the most connected files in the pipeline) orchestrates this extraction. The prescreening stage then filters simulation results against quality thresholds, discarding runs where Brutus did not converge or where numerical artifacts corrupted the data. Building on the initial conditions from Step 2, this step ensures only reliable data reaches the PINN training stage.

steps.title: Dataset Validation Framework
steps.description: The dataset readiness checks form the project's most depended-upon subsystem (fan-in leader: 16 for `datastructures.py`, 15 for `create_issue`). This structured validation framework defines data models (`datastructures.py`), a configuration system (`config.py`), format parsers (`parsers.py`), and physics validation logic (`physics_core.py`). The `__main__.py` CLI entry point and `validator.py` orchestrator run the full suite of checks -- completeness, correspondence, file format, metadata, physics, curriculum, and temporal consistency. The modular design under `modules/` allows each validation concern to evolve independently.

steps.title: PINN Framework Specifications
steps.description: The three canonical framework specs define the CTL-PINN architecture that will be trained on the validated simulation data. `ctl_instruction.md` specifies the curriculum training methodology and input-vector formulation. `pinn_architecture.md` defines the neural network backbone (SQN/SkipResNet/SIREN), the automatic differentiation contract, and the output head. `sampling_method.md` (frozen by directive) documents the IC sampling strategy that produced the existing dataset. The `ctl_pinn_resolution.md` research report records the v1.4 adjudication decisions bridging the issue documents to the framework specs.
steps.languageLesson: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) embed physical laws -- typically differential equations -- directly into the loss function. Instead of learning purely from data, the network is penalized for violating known physics, which dramatically reduces the amount of training data needed for well-posed problems.

steps.title: Project Planning and Governance
steps.description: The `.planning/` directory houses the project's structured governance artifacts. `REQUIREMENTS.md` captures v1.5 sourcing and scope policies (including the critical SCOPE constraints that freeze `sampling_method.md` and designate grounding sources). `ROADMAP.md` maps the milestone sequence from v1.0 through v1.5. `PROJECT.md` defines project identity and core decisions. The `codebase/ARCHITECTURE.md` provides an architectural map of the codebase structure and layer interactions.

steps.title: Development Infrastructure and CI/CD
steps.description: The project enforces rigorous development practices through automated infrastructure. GitHub Actions workflows (`gemini-dispatch.yml`) orchestrate AI-assisted code review and issue triage. The custom git hooks in `.githooks/` (commit-msg, pre-commit, pre-push) enforce commit message conventions and staged path validation. The `scripts/agent-commit` wrapper ensures AI-authored commits follow the project's conventional commit format. The `scripts/setup-git-hooks.sh` script installs these hooks for new contributors.
steps.languageLesson: Git hooks in `.githooks/` are managed via `git config core.hooksPath` rather than the default `.git/hooks/`, allowing them to be version-controlled alongside the codebase. The `setup-git-hooks.sh` script sets this configuration so hooks survive `git clone`.

steps.title: Quality Gates and Testing
steps.description: Two test suites guard project integrity. `test_phase12_validation.py` verifies the dataset readiness validation framework from Step 6 -- ensuring the data quality checks themselves produce correct results. `test_git_policy.py` enforces the governance conventions from Steps 8-9: commit message format, staged path policies, and agent commit compliance. These tests run as part of the development workflow to catch regressions before they reach the shared branch.
